title: Great location, awful hotel
text:
Terrible hotel. We paid a lot of money ($600+) for an extremely sub-standard tiny room. An “ocean view” if you stood on the balcony. The bathroom was so badly designed that the whole room flooded when you used it. Staff were condescending and rude, except for reception staff who were great.

Terrible hotel overcharging because of a wonderful location. Stay at the Quest.

ownerResponse.text: Thanks for your review, Lisa. We're pleased you enjoyed the adult only twilight sessions. Apologies about the few people who were disruptive to your experience but good on you for saying something so you could still enjoy it :) Thanks for recommending the locker to others, and arriving early to get prepared before your session. School holidays is typically a time that attracts more people with kids, so if you're after a quieter time, the evening sessions are great during school holidays. Great tip! The locker area is unisex, but we have dedicated private cubicles for showers and toilets. Thanks again for visiting, we're so pleased you stumbled across us a few weeks ago!

title: Go to the evening session if you don’t want to sit with kids
text: Only discovered that these hot springs even existed a few weeks ago!  I was researching Warrnambool for a one night stopover and was excited to book.  Even better when I saw that evening sessions are kid free.  I’ve worked in school, and have kids, but omg they would be bored here.  And naughty I’m guessing.  Most people left their phones in lockers which was excellent.  One tourist couple sat in the cave with phones out loud playing videos, so I had to Karen them.  There was a couple others whom felt that the entire world had to be third party to their conversation, but otherwise excellent.  So many pools and areas to rotate around to with varying temperatures etc.  no need for a robe or shoes in between.  Lovely calm ambiance.  I’d recommend hiring a locker for $8.00.  Arrive 15 mins beforehand to get sorted.  We were over it before the two hour session was up.  If you go during the day, especially school holidays, they allow kids over 5, so I can’t imagine how you’d ever relax.  There’s showers to rinse and change but it’s all unisex except for toilet and change cubicles.

title: Utterly Dsappointed
text:
After a three-hour drive from Melbourne, we were hoping for a relaxing stay… instead, Deep Blue Hotel delivered one of the most disappointing hotel experiences we’ve had in years.

We checked into Room 209, only to open the door and find an incredibly small, dated room that looked like it hadn’t been touched since the 1970s. The furnishings were damaged, the layout was cramped, and the overall feel was far below what you’d expect for the price. We turned around and left the room immediately.

Hoping to salvage the stay, we asked for an upgrade and were willing to pay whatever it took just to not sleep in that room. We were quoted a $40 charge for a King Suite upgrade on Level 4 (Room 413) — but when we walked in, it was the exact same outdated room, just two floors higher, now with a “view” directly into the hotel in front. No improvement. No sense of value.

For a hotel called “Deep Blue,” don’t be misled — there is nothing remotely ‘blue’ or scenic about the experience. The pool is cold, and there is no spa or sauna available unless you pay exorbitant prices to access the separate Hot Springs area. For a supposed wellness-style hotel, this is incredibly misleading.

Overall, the hotel feels overpriced, dated, tired, and in desperate need of a full refurbishment. We left feeling frustrated, disappointed, and honestly stunned that this is marketed as a premium stay. Guest parking is limited- good luck finding a car park due to the Hot Springs guests. 

Would not recommend.

title: Terrible. Stay at the Quest.
text:
Terrible. 
1. Parking (costs $10) as they don’t have enough. 
2. Room - smell was awful each time you entered.
3. Couch - was basically broken on the legs and wobbled 
4. Cheap furniture and fittings (this was supposed to be one of the penthouse suites). Didn’t resemble some of the advertised photographs.
3. Window of one bedroom and one sitting area were facing the general walking corridor where people could see in if the blinds weren’t shut. Just odd!
4. A note that states if you don’t leave used dishes washed and put back away you will be charged. Surely the dishwasher is enough. 
5. Stained carpets:
6. Cheap mattress and just a double bed in main bedroom. Oh and nowhere to put luggage off the floor.
7. Outside street noise with cars burning up and down at night and easy to hear.
8. View of the skate park. Hmmmm.
9. Toilet has never seen a bleach in its life. Grubby shower and skirting boards.
Need I go on? 

Do yourself a favour save money and the hassle and stay at the family room in the QUEST.

text:

Our room : HIGH SEA VIEW modern room with balcony, had everything we needed. The indoor swimming pool is so beautiful and it was great in it. Plus they have a buffet breakfast!!!! every morning. 
A BIG THANK YOU TO THE DEEP HOTEL & HOT SPRINGS.
